trial.title: Use of Mesenchymal Stem Cells in Pre-term Patients With Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia.

endpoints.measure: Security of MSC therapy in very low birth weight preterm babies at risk of developing bronchopulmonary dysplasia
endpoints.description: Number of patients with adverse events during the infusion time and during all study; and comorbilities due to preterm birth.
Number of days of life from birth to administration of the first dose and number of days of life in successive doses.

endpoints.measure: Incidence of BPD and PH in very low birth weight babies treated with MSC
endpoints.description: Status on week 36 of post-menstrual age

endpoints.measure: Diagnosis and stage of bronchopulmonary dysplasia on week 36 of post-menstrual age according to Jensen
Exitus on week 36 and 40 of post-menstrual age or at hospital discharge
Incidence of comorbidities resulting from prematurity from the time of screening to 40 weeks' EPM, hospital discharge or death.
endpoints.description: (sepsis confirmed by blood culture, treated patent ductus arteriosus, non-pharmacological ductal closure, necrotising enterocolitis, isolated bowel perforation, intraventricular haemorrhage ≥ 2, retinopathy ≥ grade 2)

endpoints.measure: Biomarker analysis (IL-1beta, IL-6, IL8, TGF beta, TNF alfa, GM-CSF, NLRP3, RAGE, HMGB1, VEGF, HGF, GREMLIN1, sVEGFR1, SP-D, SMPD1, SMPD3, IsoPs, IsoFs, NeuroPs, NeuroFs, miRNAs).
endpoints.description: biomarkers will be measured in pg/ml

endpoints.measure: Variations in echocardiographic parameters of pulmonary hypertension (PH) before and after mesenchymal cell therapy.
endpoints.description: NO PH (type I less 35%), MILD PH (type I-II between 35-50%) , MODERATE PH (type II between 50-70%) and SEVERE PH ( type II-III, more than 70%)

endpoints.measure: Changes in modified respirator score during therapy and up to week 36 of port-menstrual age
endpoints.description: 0 - 13 (min- max value). Higher score means worse outcome.

endpoints.measure: Changes in Respiratory Severity Score (RSS) during therapy and up to week 36 of port-menstrual age
endpoints.description: 0-30 (min- max value). Higher score means worse outcome.

endpoints.measure: Date of hospital discharge and respiratory care at discharge.
endpoints.description: Date of hospital discharge and respiratory care at discharge.

endpoints.measure: Need for supplemental O2 at home discharge and during follow-up (Number if patients that need supplemental O2).
endpoints.description: Number if patients that need supplemental O2

endpoints.measure: Duration of invasive and non-invasive mechanical ventilation.
endpoints.description: Duration of invasive and non-invasive mechanical ventilation.
For the treatment or prevention of BPD
Evaluation of cognitive developement, languaje developement and motor developement.

outcome.rationale: Phase 2 trial with safety/feasibility primary endpoints likely to succeed based on prior Phase I data. Efficacy on secondary endpoints plausible but uncertain given limited sample size (n=75) and wide confidence intervals. Dose-response comparison (3 vs 6 infusions) is novel with no prior data. Overall trial expected to meet primary safety/feasibility endpoints but efficacy results will be hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

analysis_trace.finding: Phase 2 randomized trial of allogeneic fetal MSC from umbilical cord for BPD prevention in very low birth weight preterm infants (≤1250g, ≤28 weeks GA). Three arms: control, 3 infusions, 6 infusions of 5x10^6 cells/kg. Expected completion December 2025.
High-risk preterm infants on mechanical ventilation with FiO2≥0.3 at days 5-14. Similar to prior Phase I/II trials by Chang et al. Population well-defined with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria.

MSC therapy aims to modulate inflammation, promote alveolarization, reduce pulmonary hypertension via paracrine effects. Multiple doses (3 vs 6) test dose-response. Allogeneic umbilical cord source used.

Primary endpoints: safety/feasibility (not efficacy). Secondary endpoints include BPD incidence/severity, pulmonary hypertension, respiratory scores, hospital discharge, neurodevelopment. No formal efficacy hypothesis testing for primary endpoints.

Based on prior Phase I trials (Chang 2013, 2022), MSC therapy in preterm infants shows acceptable safety profile with no serious infusion-related adverse events. Expected AE rate: 10-20% mostly mild-moderate.
Risk of pulmonary hemorrhage, hemodynamic instability, immune reactions. Phase 2 may show higher AE rates than Phase I due to larger sample (n=75). Multiple infusions may increase cumulative risk.

Direct evidence: Phase I trials demonstrate safety and feasibility. Indirect: Phase II trial (Stem Cells Transl Med 2021) showed efficacy signals. No direct results for this specific trial (expected 2025). Predictions based on mechanism and prior trials.
No direct outcome data for NCT06270199 available before cutoff. Dose comparison (3 vs 6 infusions) is novel; no prior data on optimal dosing regimen. Long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes uncertain.
